newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-CAPOBIANCO CONDEMNS IAAF DELAY ON DRUG HEARING.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CAPOBIANCO CONDEMNS IAAF DELAY ON DRUG HEARING.

text.p: Dean Capobianco, the Australian sprinter at the centre of a drug controversy at the Atlanta Olympics, has criticised the International Amateur Athletic Federation for the delay in setting a date for his arbitration panel hearing.

"It is dragging on and the IAAF do not seem to have considered it very important from the start but I still have to clear my name in the eyes of the Australian public," said Capobianco in a telephone interview from his training base in Bedford, England.
"The IAAF do not seem to consider the athletes very much. A lot of questions have been asked of me in the last few months and its about time that the IAAF were asked about what happened."

Traces of the steroid stanozolal were found when Capobianco was tested at a meeting in Hengelo, Holland, in May. He subsequently competed in Atlanta after his national federation, Athletics Australia, found the collection procedures in Hengelo were seriously flawed and cleared him.

The Athletics Australia management board meets in Melbourne on Sunday discuss the athlete's demand that the Australian federation pays his legal costs, estimated by his manager John Bicourt to stand at $70,000.
IAAF spokesman Giorgio Reinari admitted there had been problems assembling an arbitration panel.
"I do not think that the arbitration panel will meet before October. We might be able to announce when it will be at the Calendar Congress in Dublin (which starts October 9)," he said.
